div.l: With hym þ̉ere was a plowman̄ þᵗat was his brother
That had y ladde of dong full many a fother
And a true swynker and a gode was he
Lyuyng in pes and perfite charite
God loved he best with all hise herte
At alle tymes though he gamed or smerte
And than his neybor right as hym selve
He wold thressh and therto dyke and delve
For crystes sake for eủery pore wight
With out hyre if it lay in his myght
His tithes payed he full faire and weel
Bothe of his ꝓpropre swynk and of his Catell
In a tabard he rode vp on a Mere
Ther was also a Reve and a Millere
A somenoᵘur and a pardon̉ere also
A manciple and my self þ̉ere wer no mo
The Miller was a stoute Carle for the nones
Full bygg he was of braun and eke of bones
Þat ꝓproued weel for ouer all þ̉ere he cam
At wrostelyng he wold bere a wey the Ram
He was short shuldred a thyk gnarre
Þ̉ere was no dor but he wold heve it of harre
Or breke it at a rennyng with his hede
His berd as any sowe or Fox was reede
And ther to brode as if it were a spade
Vpon þe cop right on his nose he hade
A wret and ther on stode a tuft of herys
Rede as the brustelys of a sowys l Erys
His nose thirles blak were and wyde
A swerd and bokeler bar he by his syde
His mouth as gret as was a gret furneys
He was a Iangeler and a golyardeys
And þat was moost of synne and of harlotryes
Weel coude he stele corn and tolle it thryes
And yet he had a thombe of gold parde
A white cote and a blew hood wered he
A bagpype weel coude he blowe and sowne
And ther with all he brout vs out of towne
A gentyl mancyple was ther of a temple
Of whiche alle Catours myght take exemple
For to be wyse in beying of Vitaile
For wheder he þat he payed or toke by tayle
All gats he wayted so in hise achate
Þat he was ay byforn̄ and in gode estate
Now is it nat þat of god a full fair gᵃrace
That suche a lewde mannys wit shal pace
Þe wisdom of many lerned men
Of maistres had he moo than thries ten
That were of lawe experte and curyous
Of whiche ther was a dozen in that hous
Worthy to be Stywardes of Rente and londe
Of eny lord that is in Englond
To make hym lyve by his ꝓpropre good
In honour detles but if þat he wer wood
Or lyve as skarsely as hym lust desire
And able for to helpen̄ all a shire
In any caas þat myght falle or happe
And yet this Manciple set ther alders cappe
The Reve was a slender coleryk man̄
His berd was shaven̄ as nygh as eủere he can̄
Hise herys was by his erys full rounde y shorn̄
His toppe was dokked like a preest by forn̄
Full long wer his leggys and full lene
All lyke a staf ther was no calf y sene
Weel coude he kepe a garner or a bynne
Ther was none Auditoᵘur coude on hym wynne
Weel wyst he by the drought or by the reyne
The yeldyng of his seed or and of his greyne
His lordys sheep hise nete and his deyrye
His swyne his hors hise hors and hise pultrye
Was holly in this Reves goủernyngg
And by his comenaūnt yaf the rekenyngg
Syn þat his lord was xxᵗⁱ yeer of age
Ther coude no man bryng hym in Arrerage
Ther ne was baylif ner herde nor other hyne
That he ne knewe his sleight and covyne
They wer a dred of hym as of the deth
Hise wonyng was full faire vpon an heth
With grene trees y shadewed was hise place
He coude better thanne his lord purchace
Full riche he was astored pryuely
His lord he coude weel plesen subtely
To geve and lende hym of his owen gode
And have a thank and yet a cote and an hode
Hym thought he had a lerned a gode mystre mystre myster
He was a good wright and a full gode Carpenter
This Reve sat vpon̄ a full good stotte
That was all pomely grey and highte scotte
